title: Minimum Additions to Make Valid String
spaceBreakdown:
- string pat: constant size 3 → O(1)
- int ans, j: scalars → O(1)
- not counted: input string word
approach: Walk through `word` while cycling a pointer over the repeating pattern `"abc"`. For each character of `word`, if it doesn't equal the current expected pattern character, that character must be inserted (count it and advance only the pattern pointer); when they match, advance both. After consuming all of `word`, complete the final `"abc"` group by adding `(3 - j) % 3` characters. This is optimal because every existing character is placed in the earliest valid slot of the repeating `"abc"` sequence, and any insertion we count is forced.
hints: A valid string is just `"abc"` repeated. As you read `word` left to right, what determines which position (a, b, or c) within a group each existing letter must occupy, and what does a mismatch with that position force you to do?

Use two pointers: one over `word`, one cycling through `"abc"`. For `word = "b"`, the pattern starts at `'a'`, mismatches (count 1, advance pattern to `'b'`), then matches and advances; finish the group afterward.

```
j = 0, ans = 0
for c in word:
    while pattern[j] != c:
        ans += 1
        j = (j + 1) mod 3
    j = (j + 1) mod 3
ans += (3 - j) mod 3
return ans
```

**Smallest input** - single character needs a full group around it.
`Input: word = "a"` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the final `(3 - j) % 3` term → returns `0`.

**Already valid** - no insertions needed, group boundary must be detected.
`Input: word = "abc"` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: always adding `1` after the loop "to close the group" → returns `1`.

**All equal** - each identical letter starts a new group.
`Input: word = "aaa"` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: advancing `j` on mismatch instead of only on match → returns `3`.

**Reverse order** - letters arrive in descending group position.
`Input: word = "cba"` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: starting pattern pointer at index `1` (`'b'`) instead of `0` → returns `4`.

**Trailing partial group** - last matched char is `'a'`, leaving `'b'`,`'c'` missing.
`Input: word = "c"` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: using `j` directly as the trailing count instead of `(3 - j) % 3` → returns `0`.

followUps.q: Instead of inserting, you may also delete characters. What is the minimum total edits to make `word` valid?
followUps.a: Use DP over positions of `word` and positions in the repeating `"abc"` cycle: `dp[i][j]` = min edits to process `word[0..i]` ending aligned with pattern index `j`. Transition either deletes `word[i]` or matches/inserts. Time O(n), space O(1) with rolling rows.

followUps.q: The target pattern is an arbitrary given string `p` (not necessarily `"abc"`). How does the solution change?
followUps.a: Replace the constant `"abc"` with `p` and cycle `j` modulo `|p|`; the trailing completion becomes `(|p| - j) % |p|`. Time O(n·|p|) worst case if mismatches are frequent, space O(1).

followUps.q: `word` arrives as a stream of unknown length with only O(1) memory. Report the running minimum insertions so far.
followUps.a: Keep `j` (current pattern index) and a running `ans` counter; on each new character, run the same mismatch loop, then expose `ans + (3 - j) % 3` as the current answer. Time O(1) amortized per character, space O(1).
